chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Hamdan al-Qalanisi from Isḥāq ibn Bunnān from Ibn Baqqāḥ from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when the husband who made an oath of abstention refused to divorce, would make for him a pen of reeds and give him a quarter of his sustenance until he divorced.

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Oath of abstention from sexual relations with one's wife
key_terms.حَظِيرَة: A pen or small enclosure, used here for separate dwelling

ai.seo_question: What is the legal procedure when a husband takes an oath of abstention (Ila) and refuses to divorce his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the practical enforcement of *Ila* by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating the judicial mechanism where a recalcitrant husband is isolated in a 'hazirah' (a reed enclosure) and given a quarter of his sustenance to pressure him into divorce. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the judge's active role in resolving marital stalemates when the husband delays, ensuring the wife's rights are protected through economic and social incentives rather than immediate forced separation.
